This short vignette focuses on the core concepts that enable reproducible,
incremental rebuilding with `stamp`: builders, plans, and rebuilds. It complements
`vignettes/stamp.Rmd` by isolating patterns and best practices you should follow
when registering programmatic targets.

```{r setup}
# Use development build when interactive *and* explicitly enabled via env var.
dev_mode <- (Sys.getenv("DEV_VIGNETTES", "false") == "true")

if (dev_mode && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  pkgload::load_all(
    export_all = FALSE,
    helpers = FALSE,
    attach_testthat = FALSE
  )
} else {
  # fall back to the installed package (the path CRAN, CI, and pkgdown take)
  library(stamp)
}
library(data.table)
set.seed(123)
```

## Key concepts

- Builder: a function registered with `st_register_builder(path, builder_fn)`.
  Signature: `function(path, parents)`. It must return a list with at least:
  - `x`: the object to save
  - optional `code`: producing function(s) used to compute the saved code hash
  - optional `code_label`: a short tag used in sidecars

- Plan: the result of `st_plan_rebuild()`. The legacy route inspects recorded
  parents and artifact presence; it is not complete requested-calculation proof.
  Explicit requests below add declared component, semantic and execution proof.

- Rebuild: executing the plan with `st_rebuild(plan)`. `st_rebuild()` calls the
  registered builders and then `st_save()` for each produced artifact, recording
  new versions and sidecars.

## Minimal example (single-target)

```{r single-target, eval=FALSE}
# Suppose we have a summary target path
summary_path <- "outputs/welfare_summary.qs2"

# Register a simple builder that loads parents and returns x+code
st_register_builder(summary_path, function(path, parents) {
  # Load welfare parents (illustrative — adapt to your parents layout)
  welfare_paths <- vapply(
    parents,
    function(p) grepl("welfare", p$path),
    logical(1)
  )
  welfare_list <- lapply(parents[welfare_paths], function(p) st_load(p$path))

  # Load macros (shared parents)
  cpi_tbl <- st_load("data/macro/cpi.qs2")
  gdp_tbl <- st_load("data/macro/gdp.qs2")
  pop_tbl <- st_load("data/macro/population.qs2")

  # call a pure worker that accepts pre-loaded inputs
  out <- bar(welfare_list, cpi_tbl, gdp_tbl, pop_tbl)

  list(
    x = out,
    code = list(bar = bar),
    code_label = "aggregate_welfare"
  )
})

# Inspect plan (strict mode is conservative)
plan <- st_plan_rebuild(
  targets = summary_path,
  include_targets = TRUE,
  mode = "strict"
)
plan

# Run only if you're ready
# st_rebuild(plan)
```

## Multi-function `code` metadata

If your target depends on multiple functions (e.g. `bar()` calls helpers
`h1()` and `h2()`), include them explicitly in `code` so `st_save()` computes a
combined hash that changes if any helper changes:

```{r code-multi, eval=FALSE}
# Good: include all contributing functions
st_save(
  x,
  summary_path,
  pk = c("country", "year"),
  parents = parents,
  code = list(bar = bar, h1 = h1, h2 = h2)
)
```

This records producing code for save comparisons. To select work against current
helper/constants/rules before execution, use explicit requests below.

## Legacy Modes: Strict And Propagate

- `mode = "strict"` selects immediate recorded parent-version mismatches.
- `mode = "propagate"` also schedules their recorded downstream descendants.

These modes apply when `requests = NULL`; neither discovers current calculation
dependencies. Request-aware selection uses the explicit graph and rechecks each
candidate after actual parent execution.

## Tips & best practices

- Prefer pure worker functions that accept inputs as arguments. It makes testing
  and registration easier.
- Register builders that use the `parents` argument; avoid global state when
  possible.
- Include helper functions in `code` metadata so any relevant change invalidates
  dependent artifacts.
- Keep builders deterministic and side-effect free (don't write inside builder;
  instead return `x` and let `st_rebuild()` call `st_save()`).

## Try it locally

To try the examples interactively, set `eval = TRUE` in the setup chunk and run
examples inside an interactive R session. Use a short `root_dir` to avoid
Windows PATH length issues.


## Appendix: example plan interpretation

A plan is a data frame with path, level and reason columns. Request-aware plans
also carry request/decision/receipt fields and preview state. Inspect the rows,
but regenerate the plan after changing recipes instead of editing its internals.

Example (pseudo-inspection):

```{r plan-inspect, eval=FALSE}
plan <- st_plan_rebuild(targets = summary_path, include_targets = TRUE)
# Show targets that are stale
plan[c("path", "reason")]
```

## Request-Aware Execution

A request declares exact parent pins, physical format, semantic metadata and
result-affecting component digests. Stamp canonicalizes paths/order and validates
retained bytes. The caller must declare every known helper, constant and rule;
stamp does not discover hidden closure dependencies. Source SHA/label alone is
not complete proof. Optional `audit` identities do not affect request equality.

This runnable root example hashes actual code formals/body under the caller's
`r-formals-body-v1` contract. Constants use a fixed-order named list with exact R
types (`r-values-v1`). The builder invokes that same calculation.

```{r requested-root, eval=TRUE}
library(stamp)
local({
  root <- tempfile("stamp-request-")
  dir.create(root)
  on.exit(unlink(root, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  alias <- basename(root)
  st_init(root, alias = alias, verbose = FALSE)
  old <- st_opts(.get = TRUE)
  on.exit(suppressMessages(do.call(st_opts, old)), add = TRUE)
  st_opts(versioning = "content", retain_versions = Inf, meta_format = "json")
  seed <- 1:3
  offset <- 2L
  helper <- function(x, offset) x + offset
  calculate <- function() helper(seed, offset)
  component <- function(value, schema) {
    list(hash = st_hash_obj(value), algorithm = "siphash13", schema = schema)
  }
  code_record <- function(fun) list(formals = formals(fun), body = body(fun))
  request <- list(
    schema = 1L, path = file.path(root, "requested.rds"),
    root = TRUE, parents = list(),
    required_components = c("calculation", "helper", "constants"),
    components = list(
      calculation = component(code_record(calculate), "r-formals-body-v1"),
      helper = component(code_record(helper), "r-formals-body-v1"),
      constants = component(list(seed = seed, offset = offset), "r-values-v1")
    ),
    semantic_schema = list(rule = list(
      type = "character", shape = "scalar", required = TRUE,
      nullable = FALSE, allow_na = FALSE
    )),
    semantic = list(rule = "add-v1"), format = "rds"
  )
  builder <- function(path, parents) {
    list(x = calculate(), metadata = list(rule = "add-v1"))
  }
  plan <- st_plan_rebuild(request$path, include_targets = TRUE,
    requests = list(request))
  plan[c("decision", "reason")]
  st_rebuild(plan, rebuild_fun = builder, dry_run = TRUE) # no invocation/writes
  st_rebuild(plan, rebuild_fun = builder)
  st_execution_info(request$path, alias = alias)[c("state", "receipt_id")]
  repeat_plan <- st_plan_rebuild(request$path, include_targets = TRUE,
    requests = list(request))
  st_rebuild(repeat_plan, rebuild_fun = builder) # satisfied: skip, no writes
})
```

Non-roots use `root = FALSE` and
`parents = list(list(path = ..., version_id = ...))` with validated persisted
byte references. A NULL pin is permitted only for an explicit selected parent
recipe; it resolves before the child executes. Supply an unnamed request list
with unique normalized paths, including each target when `include_targets = TRUE`.

Plans show run/skip/blocked candidates but are not execution records. Rebuild
revalidates after actual parent results. `st_is_stale(request = ...)` raises
`stamp_blocked_request` on blocked proof, rather than reporting currentness.
`st_should_save(request = ..., x = result)` only compares supplied results for
saving; neither it nor an unchanged raw save proves a builder executed.

### Retained Output And Failures

After A1 becomes A2, B must actually execute against A2. Equal sanitized content,
producing code, complete component proof, semantic schema/values and format allow
B to retain B1 with a new execution receipt binding A2. Original B1 sidecars/A1
provenance stay unchanged; C rechecks and skips against the same B1. Changed B
component or semantic proof creates a new version even for equal result data.
A fully satisfied repeat creates neither a version nor an execution receipt.

Deterministic failures require both changed input/component proof and
`request$review = list(outcome_id = <governing failure ID>)`. Review alone,
source audit or semantic/format-only edits do not permit recovery. Blocked
observations do not replace actual failures. External failures permit one
attempt on the next analyst-started rebuild; unknown actual failures stay
blocked. Builder errors may declare `stamp_deterministic_failure` or
`stamp_external_failure`. Missing builder registration is a recoverable
configuration block, not an actual unknown execution failure. No Force or
automatic retry is provided.

`st_record_outcome()` records only failed/blocked facts, never success.
`st_execution_info()` and pinned sidecar reads are data-free (byte checksum
streaming is allowed), and explicit IDs never fall back to current metadata.
Committed references protect outputs, effective inputs and original retained
ancestry from pruning; inspect `st_prune_versions(..., dry_run = TRUE)` first.
These are serial isolated-execution guarantees, not SMB atomicity, multiwriter
safety or cryptographic authenticity.

## Typed Semantic History

Descriptors declare type, shape, required, nullable and allow_na. Integers and
doubles, optional absence, NULL, typed NA and empty vectors remain distinct.
Scalar means length one; vector permits zero or more values. Classed/nested
values, NaN and infinities are rejected. The following example needs QS2 for
the `both` sidecar mode.

```{r typed-history, eval=TRUE}
library(stamp)
local({
  root <- tempfile("stamp-metadata-")
  dir.create(root)
  on.exit(unlink(root, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  alias <- basename(root)
  st_init(root, alias = alias, verbose = FALSE)
  old <- st_opts(.get = TRUE)
  on.exit(suppressMessages(do.call(st_opts, old)), add = TRUE)
  st_opts(versioning = "content", retain_versions = Inf, meta_format = "both")
  schema <- list(
    count = list(type = "integer", shape = "scalar", required = TRUE,
      nullable = FALSE, allow_na = FALSE),
    weights = list(type = "double", shape = "vector", required = FALSE,
      nullable = TRUE, allow_na = TRUE)
  )
  first <- st_save(1:3, "typed.rds", alias = alias, verbose = FALSE,
    metadata = list(count = 1L, weights = numeric(), note = "first"),
    semantic_schema = schema)
  second <- st_save(1:3, "typed.rds", alias = alias, verbose = FALSE,
    metadata = list(count = 1L, weights = NULL, note = "second"),
    semantic_schema = schema)
  st_read_sidecar("typed.rds", alias, first$version_id)$weights # numeric(0)
  st_read_sidecar("typed.rds", alias, second$version_id)$weights # NULL
  same <- st_save(1:3, "typed.rds", alias = alias, verbose = FALSE,
    metadata = list(count = 1L, weights = NULL, note = "description edit"),
    semantic_schema = schema)
  same[c("skipped", "version_id")] # descriptions are not rewritten
  st_execution_info("typed.rds", alias = alias)$state # raw saves: absent
})
```

Semantic/schema changes create immutable versions even for equal data;
descriptive-only unchanged saves are ignored. JSON/QS2/both preserve declared
types; contradictory modern sidecars block. Legacy descriptive lists are not
reinterpreted. Modern metadata names must be unique and cannot collide with
stamp-owned names such as path, format, parents, attrs or execution.

Pinned `st_read_sidecar(version_id = ...)` errors on missing required historical
proof instead of substituting current metadata, without loading artifact data.
`st_load_version()` uses the physical format recorded in the exact snapshot when
metadata are available, even if it overrides the extension or current format.
Legacy compatibility permits extension/default data recovery when metadata are
unavailable. This neither repairs metadata nor certifies execution proof; any
readable modern marker requires strict pinned metadata validation.
